title: Pooled capacity migration sprint proposal
content:
Purpose:
- Proposal for a 4-week solutions-eng sprint to validate a migration pattern from hosted-first to regionally segmented pooled dedicated capacity with private pockets for regulated data. Goal is to deliver a small reproducible demo, a cost/provisioning ledger, and an ops runbook for customer handoff.

Background / customer archetype:
- Mid-market fintech (KYC + payments) with multi-region presence (EU + US) and upcoming APAC pilot.
- Current constraints: data residency requirements for EU ledger data, low 50–100ms p95 latency requirement for customer-facing chat, and bursty nightly batch generation for reporting.
- Wants cloud-managed experience but must certify audit controls for EU data.

Sprint objectives (measurable):
1) Deliver a working topology that routes EU-pii traffic to dedicated EU pools (or private endpoints) while non-PII traffic uses hosted or pooled global capacity.
2) Produce a cost model (monthly) for 3 scale points: pilot (5k req/day), steady (100k req/day), growth (1M req/day).
3) Create an ops runbook for autoscaling, failover to hosted, and incident steps for SLA misses.
4) Determine feasibility of maintaining <75ms p95 under steady load for EU dedicated pool.

Constraints & non-goals:
- Non-goal: full on-prem turnkey delivery (we will demo a private VPC package for 1 rack equivalent but not a permanent air-gapped install).
- Compliance constraint: EU-regulated documents must not traverse non-EU-managed memory/storage.

Architecture options considered (summary):
A) Hosted-first with regional routing (lowest time-to-value)
  - Pattern: keep default on hosted API; use routing policy that pins EU tokenized traffic to hosted region eu-west with stricter retention and KMS policy.
  - Pros: fastest to demo, minimal ops overhead, good for bursty workloads.
  - Cons: risk if customer requires dedicated hardware or explicit private tenancy; slightly higher predictable cost per sustained throughput.

B) Dedicated pooled capacity (recommended for many mid-market customers)
  - Pattern: provision dedicated GPU pool per region (eu, us). Route sensitive traffic to regional pools. Fallback policy: if dedicated pool saturated, fallback to hosted with throttling/alerts.
  - Pros: predictable latency and unit economics at scale, clear tenancy boundary for audits, easier SLAs.
  - Cons: commit required (cost) and longer lead time to provision GPUs. Needs autoscaling knob tuning.

C) Private pocket (VPC + optional on-prem node for sensitive subsystems)
  - Pattern: private control plane + customer VPC peering. Optional single-node on-prem bridge for extreme data residency.
  - Pros: strongest compliance posture and isolation.
  - Cons: highest ops surface area, longer instal lead time, limited autoscaling without cloud interconnects.

Tradeoffs matrix (quick):
- Time to demo: A > B > C
- Long-term unit cost (at scale): B < A < C
- Compliance guarantee: C > B > A
- Burst handling: A > B (with burst pool) > C

SLA and perf targets to validate:
- Target latency: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 75ms for text-gen short chat (max prompt + 128 tokens).
- Throughput: dedicated EU pool target 200 req/s sustained to cover steady scenario with headroom.
- Availability: aim for 99.95% for dedicated pools during demo window.

Cost ledger (back-of-envelope monthly):
- Assumptions: 1 request = 30 tokens input + 60 tokens output average. Hosted cost estimate: $0.00035 per token equivalent. Dedicated GPU amortized: 1x A100-equivalent = $18k/mo incl infra in reserved pricing, can serve ~250k tokens/hour depending on quantization.
- Pilot (5k req/day): Hosted-first: ~$160/mo. Dedicated (1 small pool): ~$5k/mo (not economical for pilot).
- Steady (100k req/day): Hosted-first: ~$3.2k/mo. Dedicated (1 region, 2 A100 equiv): ~$36k/mo (break-even depends on >500k req/day).
- Growth (1M req/day): Hosted-first: ~$32k/mo. Dedicated (3 A100 equiv + autoscaling): ~$54k–80k/mo (more cost-efficient at higher sustained volume).
- Note: numbers are intentionally coarse; exact model will be derived in sprint.

Demo plan (week-by-week):
Week 0 (pre-sprint prep): align with customer on sample dataset, confirm EU PII filter heuristics, provision test accounts and KMS keys.
Week 1: implement routing prototype: identify inbound token flags, build policy that maps flags -> region pool, smoke test on small load.
Week 2: provision small dedicated pool in eu-west, benchmark p95 latency under synthetic load (varying batch sizes and sequence lengths).
Week 3: implement fallback policy to hosted + run resilience scenarios (node drain, region failover), capture logs/tracing for RCA.
Week 4: stitch cost ledger, finalize ops runbook, deliver handoff doc and demo to customer.

Acceptance criteria (POC success):
- EU PII flagged traffic stays within eu-dedicated pool or private endpoint by policy with verifiable audit logs.
- p95 latency < 75ms at steady load test profile.
- Fallback path to hosted does not exceed 200ms p95 (for non-PII allowed traffic) and triggers an alert.
- Cost ledger produced + recommendation for next 90/180 day purchase horizon.

Operational runbook highlights (to produce during sprint):
- Autoscale thresholds (cpu/gpu utilization, qps, queue depth) and warm-start policy for new nodes.
- Eviction/fallback steps and how to toggle routing policies in console.
- Incident playbook for model OOMs, KV cache mismatches, quantization regression detection.

Open questions and risks:
- Exact EU PII classifier: who owns production-quality classifier? (Customer or Redwood-managed?)
- SLA negotiation: will customer accept split SLA (dedicated pools SLA + hosted fallback best-effort)?
- Networking: does customer have cloud interconnect or will we rely on public peering for VPC peering?
- Billing semantics: can we provide a blended invoice for hosted + dedicated usage in POC?

Next steps (action items):
- [Aisha] schedule kickoff with customer (target 2025-02-10).
- [Marco] produce synthetic load scripts and baseline harness (due 2025-01-24).
- [Evelyn] provision EU KMS sandbox and draft key rotation notes (due 2025-01-27).
- [Samir] estimate dedicated pool flavors (A100 vs H100 equiv) and draft cost scenarios (due 2025-01-28).

Notes to self / heuristics captured during workshop:
- When in doubt start hosted + gated dedicated pilot: reduces time to first value and gives telemetry to justify dedicated commit.
- Keep private pocket only for absolute-regulated artifacts; otherwise it creates too much ops friction for customers trying to move quickly.
- Instrument early: token-level traces and route-level metrics were the most convincing datapoints in prior demos.

Appendix (artifacts to attach during handoff):
- sample routing policy JSON (will be attached to Confluence page),
- load-test scripts (GH repo link above),
- cost model spreadsheet (sheet id will be attached).

End.
